explanation: At each step one half is sorted. Check whether the target belongs to that half's value range, and discard the other half accordingly.
timeComplexity: O(log n) time for n distinct values.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: With distinct values, at least one half around mid is sorted. Its endpoint range tells whether the target can occur in that half; discarding a half that excludes the target cannot remove a valid match. Repeating until equality or an empty interval therefore returns the target’s index exactly when present.
walkthrough: For [11,14,2,5,8] and target 14, the first middle value is 2. The sorted right half 2,5,8 excludes 14, so search left. That remaining half finds 14 at index 1; return 1.
edgeCases: Distinct values are required for choosing the sorted half this way.
An unrotated input works as ordinary binary search.
